newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Euro bourses hit new peaks, dollar steadies.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Euro bourses hit new peaks, dollar steadies.

text.p: Several leading European bourses, including Frankfurt, Paris and Milan, scaled new heights in morning trading on Wednesday, aided by an advance on Wall Street.

Even the London stock market, following a 2.7 percent leap on Tuesday, rose near to a new peak before slipping back to show limited gains ahead of a tough first budget from the new British Labour government in mid-afternoon.
"The budget will be much more threatening than people expect," said Charterhouse chief economist, Richard Jeffrey.
"There is enough bid speculation around to get market-makers going but the closer the budget gets, the fewer bets people will take and it tends to get very quiet on budget days," he said.
On the currency market, the dollar was regaining some strength after being hit by a rush into the yen after news of flotation of the Thai baht.
Against the mark, meanwhile, the U.S. currency was a little below the 40-month high of 1.7488 marks it reached on Tuesday but well up on the previous European close.

By mid-morning the Frankfurt bourse, gaining from the dollar's strength against the mark which signals good news for exporters, was around 0.9 percent higher on the 30-share DAX index. Paris was up around 0.5 percent and Milan 1.4 percent ahead.

In Paris, shares in Channel tunnel operator Eurotunnel were briefly suspended limit-up after jumping more than 20 percent on news that France and Britain could extend its licence to 99 years. Eurotunnel was later up 11.6 percent at 7.70 francs after an early high of 8.40.

The London stock market, Europe's busiest, rose within five points of its record level on the FTSE 100 index on the belief that it would get its wish for a tough budget to cap inflation. But then jitters ahead of the budget speech set in.

Share prices had risen on Tuesday partly on market speculation that Chancellor of the Exchequer (finance minister) Gordon Brown might not scrap Advanced Corporation Tax (ACT) relief on institutional investors' dividends -- a much tipped move which had unsettled share trading recently.
But that view was not so popular on Wednesday. "It's very unlikely he'll do nothing with ACT. Governments generally make unpopular decisions early on," said a dealer.
The British pound, meanwhile, traded around 2.8983 marks, up from 2.8880 at the previous close.
The yen became a safe haven after the Bank of Thailand said it was dropping its pegged rates system against a basket of currencies and allowing the market to set rates.
In reaction the dollar sank to a session low of 114.15 yen, although it later recovered somewhat as the surprise wore off, while staying below its previous European closing level.

"Whenever a developing currency is allowed to float, there is always some fear in the market and that causes a capital outflow, and in the Asian region the safe haven is obviously the yen," said Alessandra Stagliano, economist at Daiwa Europe.

"The fact Thailand has floated its currency could be the prelude to more countries moving, which would provide support for the yen, although that will take time to feed through," said Gerard Lyons, chief economist at DKB International.
Elsewhere, currency traders did not anticipate any change in interest rates from a meeting of the U.S. central bank's Federal Open Market Committee which ends on Wednesday.

"We don't see anything happening that might jolt the dollar out of its current range. There's no major influence coming from the FOMC and everybody seems comfortable with the dollar's recent range," Stagliano said.
Lyons said U.S. non-farm payrolls data, due on Thursday, could be of more interest to the market.
CURRENCIES AT 0945 GMT
The dollar was at 114.35 yen and 1.7465 marks, compared with 114.90 and 1.7421 in late European trade on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 0945 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 5.8 points at 4,734.1, having earlier hit 4,791.1, just below its all-time high of 4,796.0 reached in mid-June.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 14.32 points at 2,958.36 after an earlier record 2,986.09.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 36.07 points at 3,855.92 after a record 3,871.13 earlier.
PRECIOUS METALS

Gold was fixed at a 4-1/4 year low of $331.45 an ounce against $333.65 at Tuesday's close after Australian producer selling and amid market concern about possible central bank selling. Silver was down two cents at $4.65.
